The main takeaway from our work is that

, for a given primary traffic load, the secondary network is more tolerant to the primary traffic when the secondary users are allowed to have a smaller transmission power and/or when the secondary network is denser than the primary network.

the connectivity of the secondary network can be improved by increasing the secondary users' transmission range or decreasing the primary traffic load, but at the expense of increasing the average number of secondary users in a secondary user's interference range.

, for a given primary traffic load, there is always a secondary network density beyond which the secondary network becomes connected and that the secondary network can tolerate a larger primary traffic load if the secondary users have higher transmission power.
